description.p: Nothing is finished when it is written. Mari is for what comes after: reading it back, marking what is weak, and making it good.

Mark a paragraph the way you would on a printed page — good, weak, cut, come back to this. The marks stay with the writing and show in the margin, so the second read is a matter of looking rather than remembering.

When something needs rewriting, open it beside the original and work on both at once. What you cut goes to the drawer rather than nowhere, and you can take it back later if it turns out to be wanted after all.
It all lives in one file: the writing, the marks, the notes, the old versions, the plan and the drawer. Send that file to somebody and they open exactly what you see.
